{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My brother-in-law claims he 'burns everything' and can never cook for family gatherings. He's a trained chef who owned a restaurant. He cooked there for twenty years. Yet at Thanksgiving, he sits while the rest of us prepare food because he's 'just hopeless in the kitchen.'

CANDIDATE A:
My brother-in-law genuinely struggles in the kitchen—he once started a small fire making toast. He tried cooking for Thanksgiving years ago and the turkey was raw inside. Now he handles cleanup and table-setting instead. His contribution is real; cooking just isn't his skill despite wanting to help.

CANDIDATE B:
The senior engineer insisted she couldn't understand the new project management software despite weeks of training. I handled all our team's scheduling. Then I saw her consulting portfolio—she'd trained other companies on that exact software. Her confusion had an hourly rate.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:49"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both situations involve individuals who claim incompetence in a skill they actually possess, using this pretense to avoid responsibility or work."}
